prs.title: fix: address the review findings from #167
prs.body:
Follow-up to #167: fixes the findings from its review.

## Workspace volume (macOS) — `f85d661`
- **Orphan cleanup never found anything on Docker.** The `volume ls` template indexed `.Labels`, which is a string there, so the call failed and every `wrkflw-ws-*` volume leaked. Cleanup now lists by label filter and reads labels with `volume inspect`. Reproduced on local Docker.
- **Hard links came back as empty files.** `fetch` now uses tar `--hard-dereference`.
- **A kept name stayed kept forever.** Once nothing on the host goes by that name, it is released and fetched again.
- **A directory a step made read-only couldn't take its changes back.** The parent is opened for the write, and its mode restored, only when the volume holds it read-only too. Pending-write behaviour for a directory only the host locks is unchanged.
- **A preserved container's volume was removed under it.** `release` keeps a volume that stopped containers still use, and gives it up after 5 s of holds when no stopped container is involved.
- `with.args` is parsed before the volume sync, so a bad `args` doesn't leave a sync half done.

## Floating setup versions — `d0f17b7`
- The week was written as a Dockerfile comment, which doesn't change the image, so the weekly rebuild never happened. It is now part of the `RUN` line.
- `3`/`1` alone count as floating for Python and Go.
- Runtime `ENV` (such as `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`) is written into the image.

## Setup verdicts — `6515e0a`
- `setup-uv`'s `python-version` installs that Python and sets `UV_PYTHON`. `activate-environment: true`, and a version file with no `version`, are refused and reported as not run.
- A `graalpy-` release is refused.
- A conditional (`if:`) setup step that would change an earlier version is refused.
- A setup step inside a composite action is "ran" only if the image holds the version and env it asks for. Before, matching the language was enough.
- `go.mod`/`go.work` read the `toolchain` line first and keep rc/beta. `package.json` passes a full release through unchanged.

## CLI and digest — `48e040f`, `53ef341`, `e4a91f4`
- `--branch`/`--tag` without `--event` is a `push`, in both run and plan, and in the trigger prefilter.
- The digest counts pass lines with a trailing duration (CTest, Bazel). It never counts an `error:`/`fatal:`/`panic:` line as a pass.
- `gate --install-hook` writes only flags given on the command line into the hook, not values from `WRKFLW_*` env.
- `compare` gives up on `git ls-remote` after 30 s, adding `ref_unsure`.
- The MCP instructions describe both `unverified` kinds.

## Setup failures — `75cb1ce`
A job whose setup-action image can't be built is now a failed job (`JobResult::setup_failed`), for plain and matrix jobs. Before, it aborted the whole run with an error. Dependents are skipped as on GitHub.

## Job memory — `f616656`
An OOM kill no longer throws away the measurements of jobs still queued for a memory slot.

## Not changed
- **Jobs reused as `unaffected` carry no unrun actions.** Stored results already carry them; the unaffected path needs a design decision, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **CLI vs bollard engine split, root-owned files in the volume, stall watchdog covering send/fetch.** None of these could be reproduced. Root ownership is documented as matching GitHub when UIDs differ.

## Tests
New regression tests for each fix:
- volume: label listing, a hard-link rebuild, kept-name release, a read-only directory, holds by stopped containers;
- setup: floating detection, version files, setup-uv, graalpy and conditional refusals, composite judgement;
- jobs: an image build failure as a failed job, plain and matrix;
- CLI: branch/tag events (unit and CLI), hook flags, the ls-remote deadline;
- digest cases;
- queued-job measurements.

Results:
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo check --no-default-features` and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` pass locally on macOS.

`BREAKING_CHANGES.md` covers the behaviour changes, and `INDEX.md` has been regenerated.

prs.title: docs: document the React Native development warnings and the rustix bump for 0.33.0
prs.body:
## Summary

A docs pass over the `v0.32.0..HEAD` range before the 0.33.0 tag. Three gaps, markdown only.

- **`docs/configuration.md`**: `devPeerAddressWarnings` and `devLifecycleWarnings` were in the React Native README, the changelog and UPGRADING, but not in the configuration guide. They are now in the structure block and in a "Development Warnings (React Native)" section, which also names `integratorLifecycleWarnings` for hosts built on `ProtocolEngineHost`.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: a `### Changed` entry for the `rustix` 1.1.6 bump from #725. 0.32.0 was built on 1.1.5, which RUSTSEC-2026-0486 reports as unsound in its extended-attribute functions. The SDK uses `rustix` only for `flock` in the file store, so no released library was affected.
- **`docs/identity-for-integrators.md`**: six em dashes replaced, per the documentation style.

## Checked

- Every relative link and anchor in tracked markdown resolves (0 broken).
- The two guards that read documentation (`crypto_recovery_docs_state_the_unauthenticated_trigger`, the relay-URL scan) read nothing these edits touch.
- No cargo tests were run: no code changed.

The install snippets in `README.md`, `bindings/java/README.md` and `bindings/python/docker/README.md` still say 0.32.0. They are bumped after the packages publish, as in #642 and #702.

prs.title: fix(pool): two ways a pool could get stuck
prs.body:
## What

Two robustness fixes for `/pool`, found while auditing it after #8.

### A tunnel listener filled up with closed connections

`tunnel::listen` forgot a connection once its socket stopped naming a peer (`peer_addr().is_err()`). A socket the *other* end closed first still names its peer: on macOS `shutdown` fails with `ENOTCONN` and `getpeername` keeps answering. So each connection that llama-server, or the far tunnel, closed first kept its slot and its file descriptor for the life of the pool. After `MAX_OPEN` (64) of them the listener refused every new connection, on the host or the giver.

Each kept stream now carries the id of the connection it belongs to, and the handler releases them all when it ends.

### A giver could be left helping a pool that wasn't using it

An invitation sent just as a giver drops off is delivered when it comes back. The giver then starts its RPC server and answers `Ready`, but the pool has ended or launched without it, and the host ignored the answer. The giver kept the worker running and refused other pools until someone typed `/pool stop`.

The host now answers any `Ready` it won't use with `Leave`: for a pool that is gone, from someone it never asked, or from a member it stopped waiting for. A repeat from a member already in the pool still changes nothing.

## Tests

- `closed_connections_dont_fill_a_listener`: 128 connections through a tunnel pair, then checks nothing is still held. Fails on `main`, passes here.
- `a_giver_answering_a_pool_that_isnt_using_it_is_told_to_leave` and `a_giver_told_to_leave_stops_its_worker`.
- `only_those_asked_can_answer_…` used to assert the host says nothing to an uninvited `Ready`; it now expects the `Leave`.

`cargo test`: 270 pass. `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.

prs.title: chore(release): 0.33.0
prs.body:
## Summary

Cuts 0.33.0 from main at ff526708 (16 commits since v0.32.0). A minor release: nothing is removed or changed in any binding, and the UDL is untouched.

## What is in it

- **Versions.** Every carrier in the CONTRIBUTING table moves to 0.33.0: the workspace version and its eleven internal dependency versions, the five local ones in `sealed`, `leaf` and `web`, `Cargo.lock`, the tool lockfiles, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json` and its lockfile, `pubspec.yaml`, and the three notices files.
- **Changelog.** `[Unreleased]` becomes `[0.33.0] — 2026-11-11` with a summary, and 0.32.0 moves to `docs/changelog/0.32.md` with a row in both archive tables.
- **Three entries that were missing.** #713 (peer id warnings), #716 (React Native lifecycle warnings) and #717 (`ProtocolEngineHost` lifecycle hints) shipped without changelog entries. They are under Added.
- **UPGRADING.** A new §31 for the behaviour that changes without a compile error, the current-line references, and the index rows.
- **SECURITY.** The supported line is `0.33.x`.
- **Wording.** Four places that said "from the next release" now say "from 0.33.0".

## Two changes beyond the cut

- `tools/capi-fuzz/Cargo.lock` is refreshed. The copy on main is stale (`cargo metadata --locked` fails against it); no CI job builds it with `--locked`, so main stayed green.
- `docs/spec/custody.md` linked to a state-machines heading that now says "seven", not "six".

## Worth a reviewer's eye in §31

- The advice to lower `peerBurst` and `peerRatePerSec` by a third when they were sized as a hard per-neighbor ceiling, since acknowledgements now have an allowance of their own of half each.
- The note that a Kotlin caller passing `onDiagnostic` by position needs the new `integratorLifecycleWarnings` argument.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --lib --no-fail-fast`: 3,761 pass. One fails locally only, `no_shipped_file_names_a_relay`, which walks gitignored worktree checkouts on the machine it ran on.
- `cargo deny check advisories`: ok.
- React Native `npm run test:js` and `tsc --noEmit`: pass.
- The archive move is lossless: re-extracting the 0.32.0 section from the previous `CHANGELOG.md` with the same link rewrite differs from `docs/changelog/0.32.md` by one trailing blank line.
- Every relative link and anchor in every tracked markdown file resolves.

Not run locally: doctests, the rustdoc gate, the bare-metal targets and the binding suites.

## After merge

- `workflow_dispatch` dry run of the release workflow with `version: 0.33.0`.
- The `v0.33.0` tag.
- Install pins in the README and the Java, Python and Docker READMEs move from 0.32.0 once the release is published.

prs.title: fix(bindings): restore the Swift bridge build and audit dependencies on every pull request
prs.body:
## Why main is red

Every CI run on main since `7c60ff0c` (2026-11-11 08:50 UTC) has failed, six in a row. There are two unrelated causes.

**1. A new advisory against a version already in `Cargo.lock`.** RUSTSEC-2026-0486 (rustix 1.1.5, unsound xattr functions) was published between the 08:19 run, which passed, and the 08:50 run. No dependency changed in that window. `Dependency Audit` (cargo-deny) has failed on every push since.

**2. #717 merged a Swift compile error.** It added lifecycle warning calls above the single expression in `sendMessage` and `sendMessageRich` in `ProtocolEngineHost.swift`. A one-expression body returns implicitly; a body with several statements does not, so both methods lost their return value:

```
ProtocolEngineHost.swift:706:9: error: missing return in instance method expected to return 'String'
ProtocolEngineHost.swift:717:9: error: missing return in instance method expected to return 'String'
```

## Why neither was caught on a pull request

| Failure | What the pull request showed | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Advisory | `Dependency Audit` skipped on #708 and #713 to #717 | The job was gated on `Cargo.lock`, `**/Cargo.toml`, `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml`. None of those pull requests touched them. A push to main runs everything, so the audit ran for the first time after each merge. |
| Swift | `Swift Package` **failed** on #717 | The check went red at 10:23:53 UTC and the pull request was merged at 10:23:58, before `CI Result` had finished. The `main` ruleset has two rules, no deletion and no force push. It requires no status check, so the merge button stays live while checks are red or still running. |
| Swift | `iOS Unit Tests` and `Flutter Binding (iOS bridge)` **passed** on #717 | Both compile `ProtocolEngineHost.swift` with `swiftc -typecheck`. A missing return is reported by the diagnostic passes that run after type checking, so `-typecheck` accepts it. Reproduced locally: main's file passes `-typecheck` and fails `-emit-sil` with the two errors above. |

## What this changes

**Fixes**

- `rustix` 1.1.5 to 1.1.6 in `Cargo.lock`, that entry only. `cargo update -p rustix` also moved `errno`, `tempfile` and `winapi-util` from `windows-sys` 0.61 to 0.52, which nothing asked for, so the bump is the version and checksum alone and `cargo metadata --locked` accepts it. The three `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` copies are regenerated. The engine was never exposed: its only rustix calls are `flock` and `Errno` in `file_store/records.rs`, and the advisory is confined to the xattr functions.
- `return` added to `sendMessage` and `sendMessageRich`.

**So the next one is caught before the merge**

- `Dependency Audit` is no longer path-gated. It runs on every pull request and takes about a minute. The `deps` filter had no other reader and is removed.
- New `.github/workflows/audit.yml` runs `cargo deny check advisories` daily and on demand. Without it the first pull request after an advisory is published finds it, whatever that pull request changes. With it the advisory shows up on a scheduled run first.
- The three Swift bridge probes (two steps in `iOS Unit Tests`, and `ci-typecheck-flutter-ios-bridge.sh`) move from `-typecheck` to `-emit-sil -whole-module-optimization -o /dev/null`. That runs the compiler's mandatory diagnostics (missing return, use before initialisation) and still produces no binary. It is not slower: 7 s against 13 s locally for the React Native source set. `BRIDGE_MAINTENANCE.md` and `docs/bridges/swift.md` describe the new command.

## What a pull request cannot change

The Swift failure was caught. It was merged anyway because nothing blocks a merge on a red check. That is a repository setting: the `main` ruleset needs a required status check on `CI Result`, the one job that fails when any other job fails and passes when the rest pass or are skipped. Until that rule exists, everything above still depends on someone reading the checks before pressing merge.

## Verification

- `cargo deny check advisories`: `advisories ok` (it fails on main).
- The second `iOS Unit Tests` probe with `-emit-sil`: two `missing return` errors on main's `ProtocolEngineHost.swift`, clean on this branch. The same file passes `-typecheck` on main, which is the gap.
- The first probe and the Flutter script pass in the new mode (`OK: Flutter iOS bridge typecheck (3 plugin + 65 BridgeRN Swift files)`).
- `actionlint` is clean on `ci.yml` and `audit.yml`.
- `cargo test -p offline-protocol-uniffi -p offline-protocol-web`, the suites whose guards read `ci.yml`, the bridge sources and the docs by path: 319 and 89 pass. The one local failure, `no_shipped_file_names_a_relay`, is from stale checkouts under an untracked `.claude/worktrees` directory on my machine and names no file in this change.

This pull request edits `ci.yml`, so every job runs on it, including `Swift Package` and the audit.

prs.title: fix: report what a local pass didn't check, and make local runs match GitHub's
prs.body:
## Why

The first benchmark against an external repository (pallets/click, GitHub run 42384079679 at commit 10774440, 11 jobs, all green) disagreed on 11 of 11 jobs, took 9m49s against GitHub's 65 s, and reported `verified` while doing it. Every cause was generic, none of it was about click:

- `astral-sh/setup-uv` has no implementation, so the step was stubbed with "Would execute GitHub action", passed, and the job failed later with `uv: command not found`. The verdict did not mention it.
- `setup-python` built its interpreter from the deadsnakes PPA, which does not exist for `3.15t`, maps `pypy-3.11` to `pythonpypy-3.11`, has no `3.14` on the default base, and hits PEP 668 for `3.12` on noble. `python-version-file` was ignored.
- `compare` on a detached HEAD skipped the workflow with "no branch in context" instead of using the run's `head_branch`.
- Action metadata was fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com on every run, with a 20 s timeout per URL and action.yaml tried after any failure, so a slow host cost 40 s per setup step.
- The combined runtime image tag hashed only the Dockerfile text, so a rebuilt base under the same tag never rebuilt the combined image.
- The failure digest listed `PASSED` lines whose test id contains `Error:`.

## What changed

This branch grew past its first commit. Everything it ships is listed here; [BREAKING_CHANGES.md](BREAKING_CHANGES.md) has the details.

**Verdict covers unexecuted actions.** A `uses:` step whose action wrkflw cannot run now emits `ActionNotRun`, is recorded as `actions_not_run: [{step, uses}]` on `job_finished` and `run_finished.jobs`, and appears under `unverified` as `{job, step, uses, reason}`, so the run's verdict is `partial`, not `verified`. The log warns, the TUI marks the step "action not run", `compare` notes it per job, and the text printers of `run`, `gate` and `plan` describe both kinds of unverified entry. Setup actions keep their quiet "Would execute" line because they are handled by the image build.

**Python via uv, setup-uv, version files.** `setup-python` installs through `uv python install` (python-build-standalone), which covers `3.x`, `3.14-dev`, `3.13t`, `pypy-3.11` and `graalpy` with the spellings setup-python accepts, links `python`/`python3`/`pip` where steps find them, and works on any Debian/Ubuntu base. `astral-sh/setup-uv` is a setup action with its `version` input. `node-version-file`, `python-version-file` and `go-version-file` are read (pyproject `requires-python`, package.json `engines.node`, go.mod `go`, or a plain version file) like the hosted actions read them.

**`--branch` on `run` and `plan`.** The branch the event is for: what a `branches:` filter sees and `GITHUB_REF`/`github.ref_name`. Defaults to the checked-out branch. `compare` passes the run's `head_branch`, so a detached checkout of the commit works. `--event` now also sets `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` in the job instead of the workflow's first trigger.

**Action metadata cache.** SHA-pinned action metadata is cached on disk (`$WRKFLW_ACTION_CACHE_DIR`, default the user cache dir under `wrkflw/action-metadata/`; `WRKFLW_NO_ACTION_CACHE=1` disables). `action.yaml` is only tried when `action.yml` is a 404, not after a timeout.

**Combined image tag includes the base image id** via a new `ContainerRuntime::image_id`, so retagging the base rebuilds.

**Digest** `error_lines` skips lines that report a passing test.

**`--tag` on `run` and `plan`**, beside `--branch`, and the MCP tools take `branch`/`tag`. `compare` uses `--tag` when the run was for a tag. `compare` and `gate` pass global flags (`-P`, runtime, Kubernetes options) on to the runs they start. Git calls are non-interactive (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, ssh `BatchMode=yes` unless the user configured ssh).

**Workspace in a volume on macOS (default change on macOS; opt-in elsewhere with `WRKFLW_WORKSPACE_MOUNT=volume`).** Steps see the workspace in a Docker volume that is synced with the host around each step, so they get a Linux filesystem (case, invalid UTF-8 names, permissions) instead of the VM's file share. Entries the host can't hold stay in the volume and are named. `WRKFLW_WORKSPACE_MOUNT=bind` restores the bind mount. Needs `ubuntu:latest` as a helper image (`WRKFLW_WORKSPACE_HELPER_IMAGE`). `wrkflw clean` removes orphaned volumes.

**Jobs run side by side by measured memory.** When the runtime's VM limits memory, each job reserves 1.5x its measured peak + 256 MiB (at least 512 MiB) instead of an equal share; jobs never measured keep the old share. Measurements are kept in `job-memory.json` in the user cache dir (`WRKFLW_JOB_MEMORY_FILE`), only by runs that schedule by memory.

**Matrix legs that differ only in the runner fold.** A leg whose differing matrix keys are read only by `runs-on`, in the same image as an earlier leg, is reported from that leg instead of being run again. `--every-matrix-leg` runs every leg.

**Digest folds legs that fail the same tests**, and an image build or job container that fails before any step is reported as `setup_failed`, not a code failure.

**Review fixes (round six).**
- A stalled engine call no longer hangs on pipes a forked child keeps open (the Ubuntu CI failure).
- After a timeout, the workspace is copied back only if the timed-out step ran in the volume, so a host-side step's files aren't deleted.
- The matrix fold sees `matrix` reads on later lines of `if: |`/`run: |` blocks, `strategy.job-index`, and `matrix. os`, and folds nothing when `runs-on` reads the matrix by index. A reused folded leg keeps `repeated_from`. Engine-level fold tests added.
- `pip install`ed commands (`pytest`, `tox`) run by name under setup-python.
- A failed installer download (uv, nodesource, Composer) fails the image build instead of caching an image without it.
- Images for floating versions (`oldstable`, `3.x`, `>=3.10`, `lts/*`, uv `latest`) are rebuilt weekly.
- Setup steps are judged per step: a refused or superseded version is reported as not run whatever the order, and a version file with no version is refused instead of installing a default.
- A job's memory reservation never drops below its highest passing peak.
- The digest keeps error lines that only mention a pass word, and folds legs only when their other failure lines agree.
- `compare` tells an unanswered `ls-remote` apart from "no such tag" and reports `ref_unsure` instead of guessing.

**Breaking for users and library callers:**
- `verdict` turns from `verified` to `partial` for workflows with actions wrkflw doesn't run (codecov, github-script, ...). Exit codes are unchanged.
- The acceleration store's schema is 2: every stored result, local or remote, is re-run once.
- Combined images are rebuilt once (tag now includes the base image id).
- `ContainerRuntime: Sync`, new `ExecutionConfig` fields, new `ExecutionEvent::ActionNotRun`.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally (macOS); CI covers Linux, macOS and Windows.
- pallets/click re-run (Docker Desktop, release build): compare 11/11 agree, every Linux leg 2605 passed as on GitHub. Warm compare 34 s; an injected regression is caught in 51 s.
